s: The naming layer every request starts with - also a crude but powerful traffic-steering and failover tool.
w: Resolvers cache answers according to TTL. Authoritative servers return records possibly weighted/geographically/failover-ordered. Low TTLs mean faster changes but more resolver load; high TTLs mean resilience but slow propagation.
use: Basic name-to-IP resolution with sane TTLs
Failover records flipping to standby IP on health failure
avoid: Sub-minute emergency failover guarantees (resolver caches ignore you)
Per-request decisions - DNS answers live minutes in caches worldwide

props.ttl_seconds: How long resolvers may cache the answer

size.queries_per_sec: Managed DNS absorbs millions q/s; cost trivial

pat.d: Primary/secondary records where secondary answers only when primary checks fail.

pits: Low TTL everywhere melts resolver bill and adds latency - lower TTL only near migrations
Registrar lockout = total outage even if your infra is perfect - use two registrars/registrar lock
tips: Interview gold: explain why DNS failover is best-effort (caches!) and what compensates (GLB anycast, client retries)
